name: 3D Production Pipeline
description: Developed an internal 3D production pipeline combining a C/C++ 3D engine with procedural workflows

items.label: Stable real-time performance on lower-end devices

legend.engine: A web based 3D engine was developed to assess further business opportunities.
legend.website: Exclusive static 3D visuals were created to elevate client's corporate image value.
legend.infographic: The library also helped creating tailor-made infographics for clients with specific technical needs.

service.headline: Leadership wanted to turn 3D rendering into a real service
body: Up until now, a few renders had been produced, but 3D had never been a sellable part of any project. We thus decided to make it a marketable solution, but the challenge was to define what to sell, and how.

benchmark.headline: I benchmarked the agency's core industry and listed past client requests
body: I decided to define the strategy according to past demand rather than an assumed persona.
I noticed clients asked technical requests like 3D exhibits and virtual galleries or custom brand animations. Those insights helped me to define a base for the possible services to be provided.

stat.label: Of the agency's clients were in semiconductors
Clients asked for 3D enabled digital experience over the year
Major competitors already provided 3D related services

paths.headline: I proposed 2 solutions: one pragmatic, one ambitious
body: The pragmatic one was a 3D module library: it would be fast to build, easy to scale, ready for static and animated renders in the short term.

The ambitious path was a web-based 3D engine: a second priority and long-term project that matched past client requests like virtual tours and 3D galleries. This project was explicitly framed as R&D rather than a sellable solution.

focus.headline: How to choose models with efficiency?
body: I analyzed the agency's client base and narrowed the models list around the dominating field: the tech industry.
I then gathered inspiration from premium stock libraries to create a complete ecosystem of models and effects.

flexibility.headline: The library had to offer flexibility & technical accuracy
body: From experience, I knew clients cared about details like pin count and component type, so I structured the library atomically, the same logic behind web design systems, keeping every element configurable per client.
To keep every render unique and fast to produce, I created procedural systems to generate most models going from PCB to abstract patterns.

legend.procedural: Each model could quickly be adjusted according to client needs.
legend.geometry: Blender Geometry Node was used to create complex procedural structures easily adjustable.

quote.quote: The PCB shape isn't exactly like our product, also the number of pins is not right either
quote.author: Client

performance.headline: Clients worried existing 3D demos were too heavy
body: Three.js and Babylon.js demos raised concerns about losing part of the audience due to performance issues.
This recurring comment drove the stack choice for the engine: using C and WebGPU for a stricter memory control. The whole project would then be compiled to WASM for the web.

split.headline: C was memory-efficient, but slowed down development
body: To answer this, I decided to split the core and UI to trade productivity over performance.
Since the core had to be optimised for performance, I kept C and used a DOD (Data-Oriented Design) approach with an ECS (Entity Component System) architecture to optimize computation speed.

The UI on the other hand, was only used during development and debugging. Therefore, I decided to use C++ with an object-oriented approach, which led to faster iteration and access to libraries like imGui.

branding.headline: Client didn't see any added value in the renders
body: After delivering the first 3D renders, we noticed clients didn't see why a generic render was worth more than a stock image.
To answer this, I decided to integrate each client's actual branding into the renders, and provide them a short guideline on the visual and how it elevates their brand.
Providing clients with more context helped get the visuals approved for one client out of two.

legend.before: At first, client felt that the visual didn't connect well enough with their brand and industry.
legend.after: After adding their logo on the visual and providing them a short introduction of the new guidelines, the client validated the latest visual.

speed.headline: The 3D engine felt slow
body: After doing some research, I targeted two potential bottlenecks worth trying to fix.

ubo.headline: 1. Optimizing memory by sharing it across objects
ubo.body: Each object had to carry its own copy of the data, creating unnecessary memory usage and slowing down performance.

legend.before: Before, all resources duplicated data from each other.
legend.after: After, all resources shared and retrieved data from a common storage, preventing bloating data redundancy.

batch.headline: 2. Grouping objects to render for greater efficiency
batch.body: The original rendering architecture processed objects independently instead of drawing them by material, creating redundant GPU operations as scene complexity increased.

legend.before: Before, objects were processed according to their instantiation in the scene.
legend.after: After, objects were first grouped by material, leading to much less costly GPU compute.

result.headline: The results spoke for themselves
result.body: Both fixes led to clear performance improvements as well as greater scalability.

stat.label: After batch rendering meshes per pipeline

profiling.headline: Bottlenecks had to be tracked
body: To better profile the whole project, runtime debug tools were added such as live render-mode switching (boundbox, wireframe, solid, texture), a per-pass latency profiler, and a logging console built in.

impact.headline:
The library helped close 4 contracts.
The engine paid in knowledge
body: The 3D module library was reused across multiple projects for key visuals, brand revamping, and infographics. It cut the production time by 4x and the strong client feedback led to contract renewals.
The engine is still in development and currently deprioritized, but it produced WebGPU expertise that's ready to apply with Three.js when the opportunity comes up.

list.headline: Narrow efforts on 1 efficient solution rather than 2
list.challenge: The library saved real time but adoption stayed narrow (3 key visuals and 1 infographic).
list.outcome: I wish to develop a strategy to increase its adoption and use it as a means to shape the brand's whole 3D direction.

list.headline: Better assessing technical workload for greater result
list.challenge: The WebGPU engine was correctly framed as R&D from the start, which contained the risk, but I still underestimated the build time versus using existing libraries.
list.outcome: I now reconsider more closely existing solutions vs reinventing the wheel in R&D.

list.headline: Scale the solution to make it available for others
list.challenge: I'm still the only designer with the 3D skill to use the library, which caps its reach.
list.outcome: The next step would be exporting pre-rendered assets so the rest of the design team can use it without touching the 3D pipeline.
